newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fujitsu says plans to raise 64MB DRAM output.
newsitem.headline: Fujitsu says plans to raise 64MB DRAM output.

text.p: Fujitsu Ltd said on Tuesday that it plans to raise its output of 64-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips to 1.5 million units per month by the end of the 1997/98 fiscal year, from its initial forecast of one million units.
A Fujitsu spokeswoman said the revision was due to increasing demand for 64-megabit DRAM chips in personal computers.

The company believed demand would shift from 16-megabit DRAMs to 64-megabit DRAMs at a faster pace than it initially expected, she said. Fujitsu did not provide a figure for its current 64-megabit DRAM output.
